sections.title: Neural versus chemical: the fast wire and the slow broadcast

board_events.text: Two systems, one coordinated body
NEURAL: fast to switch on, brief, localised. An electrical impulse to a specific target.
Example: pulling your hand off a hot surface.
CHEMICAL: slow to switch on, long-lasting, widespread. A chemical messenger broadcast through the blood.
It acts only on cells that carry the matching receptor.

board_events.text: The hypothalamus is the junction box: brain tissue that also secretes hormones.
Integration of the two systems is exactly what this chapter's title names.

segments.text: <curious>How does your body carry a message from one place to another? It has two completely different answers, and this chapter is about how they work together.
The first is neural coordination. It is fast to switch on, it is brief, and it is localised. An electrical impulse fired down a nerve to one specific target.
Think of jerking your hand off a hot surface. You need it in a fraction of a second, at exactly one place, and then it is over. That is what a wire is for.
The second is chemical coordination. Slow to switch on, long-lasting, and widespread. A chemical messenger poured into the blood and carried everywhere.
But everywhere does not mean everyone. A hormone acts only on cells that carry the matching receptor. The blood knocks on every door; only some doors have a lock that fits.

Look at the two rows. Neural: brain, impulse, one target, finished. Chemical: gland, hormone into blood, many cells reached but only receptor-bearing cells respond. Growth, metabolism and reproduction all run on that slow broadcast.
<excited>And here is where they join. The hypothalamus is brain tissue that also secretes hormones. It is the junction box that converts a nervous signal into a hormonal command.
That conversion is the integration in the chapter's title. Neither system works alone. The body needs the instant reaction and the sustained programme, both.
<curious>आपकी body एक जगह से दूसरी जगह message कैसे भेजती है? इसके दो बिलकुल अलग जवाब हैं, और यह chapter उन्हीं दोनों के साथ काम करने के बारे में है।
पहला है neural coordination. यह switch on होने में fast है, brief है, और localised है. एक electrical impulse, नर्व से होकर, सिर्फ एक specific target तक।
सोचिए, गरम चीज़ से हाथ खींचना. वो response एक पल में चाहिए, एक ही जगह पर, और फिर खत्म. wire का काम यही है।
दूसरा है chemical coordination. Switch on होने में slow, long-lasting, और widespread. एक chemical messenger जो blood में छोड़ा जाता है और पूरे body में पहुँचता है।
लेकिन हर जगह पहुँचने का मतलब हर cell पर असर नहीं. Hormone सिर्फ उन्हीं cells पर act करता है जिनके पास matching receptor हो. Blood हर दरवाज़े पर दस्तक देता है, पर ताला सिर्फ कुछ के पास है।

दोनों rows देखिए. Neural: brain, impulse, एक target, खत्म. Chemical: gland, blood में hormone, बहुत सारे cells तक पहुँच पर respond सिर्फ receptor वाले करते हैं. Growth, metabolism और reproduction इसी slow broadcast पर चलते हैं।
<excited>और यहीं दोनों मिलते हैं. Hypothalamus brain tissue है जो hormones भी secrete करता है. यही वो junction box है जो nervous signal को hormonal command में बदल देता है।
यही conversion chapter के title वाला integration है. कोई भी system अकेला काम नहीं करता. Body को instant reaction भी चाहिए और sustained programme भी।

sections.title: What counts as a hormone: the four-gate definition

board_events.text: What is a hormone?
A NON-NUTRIENT chemical: a messenger, not food or fuel.
An INTERCELLULAR messenger: it carries a signal from cell to cell.
Secreted in TRACE amounts by endocrine tissue.
Carried by BLOOD to a distant target.
It acts only on a target that carries its specific receptor.

board_events.text: Drop any one gate and the definition breaks.

segments.text: The word hormone gets used loosely in daily life. In this chapter it has a tight definition, and every word in it is load-bearing.
Gate one: non-nutrient. It is a chemical messenger, not food and not fuel. Glucose travels in your blood and changes what cells do, but glucose is nutrition, so it is not a hormone.
Gate two: intercellular. It carries a signal from one cell to another cell. The whole point is communication between cells, not inside one.
Gate three: trace amounts, secreted by endocrine tissue. These are tiny quantities. A hormone is a signal, not a bulk supply, so a very small amount does a very large job.
Gate four: carried by blood, acting on a distant target. The messenger is released into circulation and does its work somewhere else in the body.
And then the rule that ties it together: it acts only on a target that carries its specific receptor. Receptor specificity is what turns a broadcast into an address.
So on the board: non-nutrient, intercellular, trace amounts, blood-borne, and then the receptor gate at the end deciding who actually responds.
Drop any one of these and the definition breaks. In an exam, a distractor is usually a chemical that fails exactly one gate, so check them one by one.
Hormone शब्द रोज़मर्रा में ढीले-ढाले तरीके से इस्तेमाल होता है. लेकिन इस chapter में इसकी definition बहुत tight है, और उसका हर शब्द ज़रूरी है।
पहला gate: non-nutrient. यह एक chemical messenger है, food या fuel नहीं. Glucose blood में चलता है और cells का काम बदलता है, पर glucose nutrition है, इसलिए hormone नहीं।
दूसरा gate: intercellular. यह एक cell से दूसरे cell तक signal ले जाता है. पूरा मकसद है cells के बीच communication।
तीसरा gate: trace amounts, endocrine tissue से secrete होता है. मात्रा बहुत कम होती है. Hormone एक signal है, bulk supply नहीं, इसलिए बहुत थोड़ा बहुत बड़ा काम करता है।
चौथा gate: blood से carry होकर distant target पर act करना. Messenger circulation में छूटता है और काम कहीं और जाकर करता है।
और फिर वो rule जो सबको जोड़ता है: यह सिर्फ उसी target पर act करेगा जिसके पास इसका specific receptor हो. Receptor specificity ही broadcast को address बना देती है।
तो board पर देखिए: non-nutrient, intercellular, trace amounts, blood-borne, और आखिर में receptor gate जो तय करता है कि respond कौन करेगा।
इनमें से एक भी gate हटा दीजिए तो definition टूट जाती है. Exam में distractor अक्सर वही chemical होता है जो ठीक एक gate पर fail करता है, इसलिए एक-एक करके check कीजिए।

board_events.text: Organised endocrine glands: pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, adrenal, pancreas, gonads, plus the hypothalamus.
Heart, kidney and GI tract are not classical glands, but they still secrete hormones.
So 'endocrine' is defined by how the product leaves, not by what the organ is called.
The pancreas does both: ducted digestive juice AND ductless hormones.

segments.text: Before we tour the glands one by one, we need the sorting rule that puts an organ in this chapter at all. It comes down to a single question: duct or no duct?
Exocrine glands release their products through ducts. Salivary glands, sweat glands, digestive glands. The product is piped along a tube to a surface or into the gut.
Endocrine glands are ductless. There is no tube. They pour their hormones directly into the blood, and the blood becomes the delivery system.
On the left, the ducted gland with its pipe to a surface. On the right, the ductless gland releasing straight into circulation. That one structural difference is the whole classification.
The organised endocrine glands in humans are the pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, adrenal, pancreas, and the gonads, meaning testis and ovary. Add the hypothalamus to that list.
But the list does not stop there. The heart, the kidney and the gastrointestinal tract are not classical endocrine glands, and they still secrete hormones. Students forget these and lose easy marks.
Notice what this means. Endocrine is defined by how the product leaves the tissue, not by what the organ is famous for. The heart is a pump that also happens to secrete.
The pancreas proves the point beautifully. It is a dual gland. Digestive juice goes out through a duct, while insulin and glucagon go straight into the blood from the same organ.
Glands का tour शुरू करने से पहले हमें वो sorting rule चाहिए जो तय करता है कि कोई organ इस chapter में आएगा भी या नहीं. सवाल सिर्फ एक है: duct है या नहीं?
Exocrine glands अपना product ducts से बाहर भेजती हैं. Salivary glands, sweat glands, digestive glands. Product एक tube से होकर किसी surface या gut तक जाता है।
Endocrine glands ductless होती हैं. कोई tube नहीं. वो hormones सीधे blood में डालती हैं, और blood ही delivery system बन जाता है।
बाईं तरफ ducted gland अपनी pipe के साथ. दाईं तरफ ductless gland सीधे circulation में release करती हुई. यही एक structural फर्क पूरी classification है।
Humans में organised endocrine glands हैं: pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus, adrenal, pancreas, और gonads यानी testis और ovary. और इस list में hypothalamus भी जोड़िए।

लेकिन list यहीं खत्म नहीं होती. Heart, kidney और gastrointestinal tract classical endocrine glands नहीं हैं, फिर भी hormones secrete करते हैं. Students इन्हें भूल जाते हैं और आसान marks गँवा देते हैं।
ध्यान दीजिए इसका मतलब क्या है. Endocrine इस बात से तय होता है कि product tissue से कैसे निकलता है, इससे नहीं कि organ किस काम के लिए मशहूर है।
Pancreas इसे बहुत खूबसूरती से साबित करता है. यह dual gland है. Digestive juice duct से बाहर जाता है, जबकि insulin और glucagon उसी organ से सीधे blood में।

board_events.text: Ask three questions: how fast did it start, how long did it last, how wide did it spread?
Case A is instant, brief, one limb. The answer is NEURAL.
Case B is slow to start, sustained for months, whole body. The answer is CHEMICAL.
Tempo, duration and spread decide it every time. Name them before you name the system.

segments.text: Let us turn the theory into a procedure, because this is how the idea actually gets tested. You are handed a response and asked which system produced it.
Case A: a hand jerks off a hot surface. That is the classic.
Case B: a child grows steadily taller across a year. Same body, completely different kind of event.
The diagram gives you the sorting funnel. You are reading the tempo of the response, and the two branches are already labelled for you.
Three questions, always in this order. How fast did the response start? How long did it last? How wide did it spread across the body?
Run Case A. It started instantly, it was over in a moment, and it involved one limb. Fast, brief, localised. That is the signature of an impulse down a nerve, so the answer is neural.
Now Case B. It started slowly, it sustained for months, and it touched the whole skeleton. Slow, long-lasting, widespread. That is a blood-borne messenger, so the answer is chemical.
<whisper>Here is the exam habit. Say the three words out loud before you commit: fast, brief, local, or slow, lasting, widespread. The system names itself once you have said them.
अब theory को एक procedure में बदलते हैं, क्योंकि असल में test इसी तरह होता है. आपको एक response दिया जाएगा और पूछा जाएगा कि यह किस system से आया।
Case A: गरम surface से हाथ का झटके से हटना. यह classic है।
Case B: एक बच्चा साल भर में धीरे-धीरे लंबा होता है. वही body, पर बिलकुल अलग तरह की घटना।
Diagram आपको sorting funnel देता है. आप response का tempo पढ़ रहे हैं, और दोनों branches पहले से labelled हैं।
तीन सवाल, हमेशा इसी क्रम में. Response कितनी जल्दी शुरू हुआ? कितनी देर चला? Body में कितना फैला?
Case A पर चलाइए. तुरंत शुरू हुआ, एक पल में खत्म, और सिर्फ एक limb. Fast, brief, localised. यह nerve पर impulse का signature है, तो जवाब neural है।
अब Case B. धीरे शुरू हुआ, महीनों चला, और पूरे skeleton तक पहुँचा. Slow, long-lasting, widespread. यह blood-borne messenger है, तो जवाब chemical है।
<whisper>Exam की आदत यह बनाइए. जवाब देने से पहले तीनों शब्द बोलिए: fast, brief, local या slow, lasting, widespread. बोलते ही system खुद अपना नाम बता देगा।

sections.title: Pitfalls: where the big picture goes wrong

board_events.text: Where students lose the easy marks
Trap: calling every gland endocrine. Salivary, sweat and digestive glands are EXOCRINE. They have ducts.
Trap: thinking a hormone reaches only its target. It reaches everything. Only receptor-bearing cells respond.
Trap: forgetting the hypothalamus is both neural tissue AND an endocrine source.
Trap: leaving out heart, kidney and GI tract when listing hormone sources.
'Non-nutrient' is load-bearing. Glucose travels in blood and changes cells, but it is fuel, not a hormone.
Chemical coordination is slow to START. That is not the same as weak.
Exam habit: describe tempo, duration and spread before naming the system.

segments.text: Now the pitfalls. This subtopic looks easy, which is exactly why it costs marks. Every trap here has appeared as a distractor.
First trap: calling every gland endocrine. Salivary, sweat and digestive glands are exocrine. They have ducts, so their products never enter the blood as messengers.

Second trap: thinking a hormone travels only to its target. It does not. The blood carries it past every cell in the body. Only cells carrying the matching receptor respond, and that is a very different mechanism from targeted delivery.

Third trap: forgetting that the hypothalamus is both. It is brain tissue, and it is an endocrine source. If a question asks you to list endocrine structures and you leave out the hypothalamus, you have lost the mark.
Fourth trap: an incomplete list. Heart, kidney and gastrointestinal tract secrete hormones without being classical glands. Examiners love this because it is the one line students skim past.
Fifth trap: ignoring the word non-nutrient. Glucose travels in the blood, reaches cells, and changes what they do. It fails the definition on the first gate because it is fuel, not a messenger.
And a conceptual one. Chemical coordination is slow to switch on. Slow is not weak. Growth, metabolism and reproduction are the largest programmes your body runs, and all of them are hormonal.
Carry one habit out of this subtopic. Before naming a system, say its tempo, its duration and its spread. That single sentence answers most questions of this type.
अब pitfalls. यह subtopic आसान लगता है, और इसीलिए marks काटता है. यहाँ का हर trap distractor बनकर आ चुका है।
पहला trap: हर gland को endocrine कह देना. Salivary, sweat और digestive glands exocrine हैं. उनके पास ducts हैं, इसलिए उनका product messenger बनकर blood में जाता ही नहीं।

दूसरा trap: यह सोचना कि hormone सिर्फ अपने target तक जाता है. नहीं. Blood उसे body के हर cell के पास ले जाता है. Respond सिर्फ matching receptor वाले cells करते हैं, और यह targeted delivery से बिलकुल अलग mechanism है।
तीसरा trap: यह भूल जाना कि hypothalamus दोनों है. वो brain tissue भी है और endocrine source भी. Endocrine structures की list में hypothalamus छूट गया तो mark गया।
चौथा trap: अधूरी list. Heart, kidney और gastrointestinal tract classical gland हुए बिना hormones secrete करते हैं. Examiners को यह बहुत पसंद है क्योंकि students यही line जल्दी में छोड़ देते हैं।
पाँचवाँ trap: non-nutrient शब्द को नज़रअंदाज़ करना. Glucose blood में चलता है, cells तक पहुँचता है, और उनका काम बदलता है. पर वो पहले ही gate पर fail है क्योंकि वो fuel है, messenger नहीं।
और एक conceptual बात. Chemical coordination switch on होने में slow है. Slow का मतलब weak नहीं. Growth, metabolism और reproduction body के सबसे बड़े programmes हैं, और सब hormonal हैं।
इस subtopic से एक आदत ले जाइए. System का नाम लेने से पहले उसका tempo, duration और spread बोलिए. यही एक line इस तरह के ज़्यादातर सवालों का जवाब है।

board_events.text: Route 1: releasing hormones switch ON an anterior-pituitary hormone; inhibiting hormones switch it OFF.
Examples: GnRH is a releasing hormone. Somatostatin is GH-inhibiting.
Route 1 travels through the hypophyseal portal system, a special blood link to the ANTERIOR pituitary.
Route 2: the hypothalamus MANUFACTURES oxytocin and ADH.
These travel down nerve fibres, to be stored in and released from the POSTERIOR pituitary.

segments.text: The pituitary is often called the master gland. It has a master of its own, and that is the hypothalamus, sitting at the base of the brain.
The hypothalamus controls the pituitary by two separate routes, and almost every mistake in this subtopic comes from mixing them up. So let us keep them apart from the first second.
Look at the split. Left branch goes to the anterior lobe through blood. Right branch goes to the posterior lobe down nerve fibres. Different cargo, different road, different destination.

Route one is a chemical instruction. The hypothalamus secretes releasing hormones, which switch on an anterior-pituitary hormone, and inhibiting hormones, which switch it off. Two opposite commands from the same source.
The examples to hold: G n R H is a releasing hormone. Somatostatin is a growth-hormone-inhibiting hormone. One opens the tap, the other closes it.

How do these instructions travel? Through the hypophyseal portal system, a special blood link running from the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary. Portal means blood, and the destination is anterior. Lock that pairing.
Route two is completely different. Here the hypothalamus is not instructing, it is manufacturing. It makes oxytocin and it makes A D H, itself.

Those two hormones then travel down nerve fibres, and they are stored in and released from the posterior pituitary. So the posterior lobe is a depot, not a factory. That single sentence answers a whole family of questions.
Pituitary को अक्सर master gland कहा जाता है. लेकिन उसका भी अपना master है, और वो है hypothalamus, brain के base पर बैठा हुआ।
Hypothalamus, pituitary को दो अलग routes से control करता है, और इस subtopic की लगभग हर गलती इन दोनों को मिला देने से आती है. तो इन्हें पहले सेकंड से अलग रखिए।
यह split देखिए. बायाँ branch blood से होकर anterior lobe तक. दायाँ branch nerve fibres से होकर posterior lobe तक. अलग cargo, अलग रास्ता, अलग destination।

पहला route एक chemical instruction है. Hypothalamus releasing hormones secrete करता है, जो anterior-pituitary hormone को ON करते हैं, और inhibiting hormones, जो उसे OFF करते हैं. एक ही source से दो उल्टे commands।
याद रखने वाले examples: G n R H एक releasing hormone है. Somatostatin growth-hormone-inhibiting hormone है. एक नल खोलता है, दूसरा बंद करता है।

ये instructions जाते कैसे हैं? Hypophyseal portal system से, यानी hypothalamus से anterior pituitary तक का एक special blood link. Portal यानी blood, और destination anterior. इस जोड़ी को lock कर लीजिए।
दूसरा route बिलकुल अलग है. यहाँ hypothalamus instruction नहीं दे रहा, वो खुद manufacture कर रहा है. Oxytocin और A D H वो खुद बनाता है।

फिर ये दोनों hormones nerve fibres से नीचे उतरते हैं, और posterior pituitary में store होकर वहीं से release होते हैं. तो posterior lobe एक depot है, factory नहीं. यही एक line सवालों के पूरे परिवार का जवाब है।

segments.text: The anterior pituitary, also called the adenohypophysis, secretes six hormones. Six is the number to hold, because the seventh one on most students' lists does not belong here.
The mnemonic is FLAT PiG. F for F S H, L for L H, A for A C T H, T for T S H, Pi for prolactin, and G for growth hormone. Six letters, six hormones.

One fact covers all of them: every pituitary hormone is a protein or a peptide. Not one steroid comes out of this gland. Remember that, because it decides their mechanism of action later in the chapter.
Now read the arrows. Notice how many of these do not act on tissue directly. They act on another gland. That is what makes the pituitary a master gland rather than a worker.
T S H stimulates the thyroid. A C T H stimulates the adrenal cortex. Two tropic hormones, each one command in a longer chain we will come back to when we do feedback.
L H and F S H are the gonadotropins. They act on the gonads, driving gamete formation and sex-hormone secretion. Same two hormones in both sexes, different jobs.
Prolactin is the one that acts on tissue directly: growth of the mammary glands, and milk formation. Formation is the word to underline, and you will see why in two sections.

<curious>And what about M S H? It acts on melanocytes to control skin pigmentation, but it comes from the pars intermedia, not the six. That is exactly why it is missing from FLAT PiG, and exactly why it appears in distractors.
Anterior pituitary, जिसे adenohypophysis भी कहते हैं, छह hormones secrete करता है. छह number याद रखिए, क्योंकि ज़्यादातर students की list का सातवाँ यहाँ का है ही नहीं।
Mnemonic है FLAT PiG. F यानी F S H, L यानी L H, A यानी A C T H, T यानी T S H, Pi यानी prolactin, और G यानी growth hormone. छह letters, छह hormones।
एक fact सब पर लागू है: हर pituitary hormone protein या peptide है. इस gland से एक भी steroid नहीं निकलता. यह याद रखिए, क्योंकि आगे chapter में इनका mechanism इसी से तय होगा।
अब arrows पढ़िए. देखिए कितने hormones सीधे tissue पर act ही नहीं करते. वो दूसरी gland पर act करते हैं. यही चीज़ pituitary को worker नहीं, master gland बनाती है।
T S H thyroid को stimulate करता है. A C T H adrenal cortex को. दो tropic hormones, दोनों एक लंबी chain की एक कड़ी, जिस पर feedback में लौटेंगे।
L H और F S H gonadotropins हैं. ये gonads पर act करते हैं, gamete formation और sex-hormone secretion चलाते हैं. दोनों sexes में वही दो hormones, काम अलग।
Prolactin वो है जो सीधे tissue पर act करता है: mammary glands की growth, और milk formation. Formation शब्द underline कीजिए, वजह दो sections बाद दिखेगी।
<curious>और M S H? वो melanocytes पर act करके skin pigmentation control करता है, पर वो pars intermedia से आता है, इन छह में से नहीं. इसीलिए वो FLAT PiG में नहीं है, और इसीलिए distractors में आता है।

board_events.text: Excess in childhood: GIGANTISM.
Excess in adults: ACROMEGALY.
Deficiency in childhood: PITUITARY DWARFISM.
Same hormone, same direction of error. The AGE of onset names the disorder.
The pituitary sits in a bony cavity, the sella turcica, joined to the hypothalamus by a stalk.

segments.text: Growth hormone deserves its own section, because it is the single richest source of disorder questions in this chapter.
G H, also called somatotropin, drives body growth, protein synthesis, and bone growth. One hormone, three effects, and all of them building.
Now look at the fan-out. One hormone at the top, three disorders below, and the branches are not sorted by which hormone. They are sorted by two things only: too much or too little, and at what age.
Excess in childhood gives gigantism. The child is still growing, the bones can still lengthen, so an oversupply makes the whole frame overshoot.

Excess in an adult gives acromegaly. Same hormone, same excess, but the adult skeleton can no longer lengthen the same way, so the picture that emerges is completely different and gets a different name.
Deficiency in childhood gives pituitary dwarfism. The growth drive was never delivered when it was needed, so growth never happens on schedule.
<excited>Hold the pattern, because it repeats in this chapter. Same hormone, same direction of error, and the age of onset picks the name. You will meet exactly this logic again at the thyroid.

One anatomical detail worth carrying: the pituitary sits in a bony cavity called the sella turcica at the base of the brain, joined to the hypothalamus by a stalk. That stalk is where both routes run.
Growth hormone अपना अलग section deserve करता है, क्योंकि इस chapter में disorder वाले सवालों का सबसे बड़ा source यही है।
G H, जिसे somatotropin भी कहते हैं, body growth, protein synthesis, और bone growth चलाता है. एक hormone, तीन effects, और सब building वाले।
अब यह fan-out देखिए. ऊपर एक hormone, नीचे तीन disorders, और branches hormone के हिसाब से नहीं बँटीं. वो सिर्फ दो चीज़ों से बँटी हैं: ज़्यादा या कम, और किस उम्र में।
बचपन में excess देता है gigantism. बच्चा अभी बढ़ ही रहा है, bones अभी लंबी हो सकती हैं, तो oversupply पूरे frame को overshoot करा देती है।
Adult में excess देता है acromegaly. वही hormone, वही excess, पर adult skeleton पहले की तरह लंबा नहीं हो सकता, तो तस्वीर बिलकुल अलग बनती है और नाम भी अलग मिलता है।
बचपन में deficiency देती है pituitary dwarfism. Growth drive उस वक्त मिला ही नहीं जब चाहिए था, इसलिए growth समय पर हुई ही नहीं।
<excited>यह pattern पकड़ लीजिए, क्योंकि chapter में दोहराया जाएगा. वही hormone, वही गलती की दिशा, और नाम उम्र से तय. यही logic thyroid पर फिर मिलेगा।
एक anatomical detail साथ रखिए: pituitary brain के base पर sella turcica नाम की bony cavity में बैठा है, और एक stalk से hypothalamus से जुड़ा है. दोनों routes इसी stalk से चलते हैं।

board_events.text: Oxytocin: contraction of uterine smooth muscle at childbirth.
Oxytocin also causes milk EJECTION from the mammary glands.
Prolactin FORMS milk; oxytocin EJECTS it. Different lobes, different verbs.
ADH, also called vasopressin: promotes water reabsorption by the kidney.
ADH also raises blood pressure by constricting arterioles. Deficiency gives diabetes insipidus.

segments.text: The posterior pituitary, the neurohypophysis, is the lobe most often described wrongly, so let us start with what it is not.
It stores and releases two hormones. It does not make them. Both were manufactured upstream in the hypothalamus and sent down nerve fibres. The posterior lobe is a depot.
Follow the picture top to bottom. Made in the hypothalamus, carried down the fibres, stored in the posterior lobe, then released into the blood to do two entirely unrelated jobs.
First hormone: oxytocin. It causes contraction of the uterine smooth muscle at childbirth. That is why it is called the birth hormone.
Oxytocin has a second action: milk ejection from the mammary glands. Ejection, meaning the milk that already exists is pushed out.

<whisper>And here is the pairing examiners love. Prolactin forms the milk, from the anterior lobe. Oxytocin ejects the milk, from the posterior lobe. Different lobes, different verbs, and the verb is the whole answer.
Second hormone: A D H, also called vasopressin. It promotes water reabsorption by the kidney, so water that would have left in the urine is pulled back into the body.

A D H has a second action too: it raises blood pressure by constricting arterioles, which is where the name vasopressin comes from. And its deficiency gives diabetes insipidus, large volumes of dilute urine. We will work that case next.
Posterior pituitary, यानी neurohypophysis, वो lobe है जिसे सबसे ज़्यादा गलत बताया जाता है. तो शुरू करते हैं इससे कि यह क्या नहीं है।
यह दो hormones को store और release करता है. बनाता नहीं. दोनों ऊपर hypothalamus में बने और nerve fibres से नीचे भेजे गए. Posterior lobe एक depot है।
तस्वीर को ऊपर से नीचे पढ़िए. Hypothalamus में बना, fibres से नीचे आया, posterior lobe में store हुआ, फिर blood में release होकर दो बिलकुल अलग काम करता है।
पहला hormone: oxytocin. यह childbirth के वक्त uterine smooth muscle में contraction कराता है. इसीलिए इसे birth hormone कहते हैं।
Oxytocin का दूसरा action है milk ejection, mammary glands से. Ejection यानी जो दूध पहले से बना है उसे बाहर धकेलना।
<whisper>और यह जोड़ी examiners को बहुत पसंद है. Prolactin दूध बनाता है, anterior lobe से. Oxytocin दूध निकालता है, posterior lobe से. अलग lobes, अलग verbs, और verb ही पूरा जवाब है।
दूसरा hormone: A D H, जिसे vasopressin भी कहते हैं. यह kidney से water reabsorption कराता है, यानी जो पानी urine में निकल जाता, वो वापस body में खींच लिया जाता है।

A D H का भी दूसरा action है: arterioles को constrict करके blood pressure बढ़ाना, और यहीं से नाम vasopressin आया. और इसकी deficiency देती है diabetes insipidus, यानी बहुत ज़्यादा dilute urine. अगला case यही है।

board_events.text: Step 1: two disorders carry the name 'diabetes'. Separate them first.
Step 2: diabetes mellitus requires HIGH blood glucose with glycosuria. Normal glucose rules it out.
Step 3: what is being lost here is water, not sugar.
ADH promotes water reabsorption by the kidney. Without it, the kidney cannot hold water back.
Answer: ADH deficiency, giving diabetes insipidus, a posterior pituitary disorder.

segments.text: Here is a N E E T-style case. A patient passes large volumes of dilute urine and is thirsty. Blood glucose is normal. Identify the problem.
Underline that second line before you do anything else. Blood glucose is normal. In a question this short, a normal value is never decoration. It is the discriminator.
The diagram lays out the two tests. Left panel: what the glucose value rules out. Right panel: what is actually being lost. Work them in that order.
Step one. Two different disorders carry the word diabetes, and they share almost nothing except the symptom of passing a lot of urine. Separate them before you go further.
Step two. Diabetes mellitus is an insulin problem, and it requires high blood glucose with glycosuria, thirst, and frequent urination. The glucose here is normal, so mellitus is ruled out.
Step three. Ask what is actually leaving the body. The urine is dilute, so it is mostly water. The patient is losing water, not sugar. That reframes the whole question onto water handling.

Which hormone handles water? A D H promotes water reabsorption by the kidney. Take it away and the kidney cannot pull water back, so it dumps large volumes of dilute urine, and the thirst follows the loss.
So the answer is A D H deficiency, giving diabetes insipidus, and its source is the posterior pituitary. Notice that the normal glucose did all the work. Read the value that seems boring.
यह एक N E E T-style case है. एक patient बहुत ज़्यादा dilute urine pass कर रहा है और उसे प्यास लग रही है. Blood glucose normal है. Problem पहचानिए।
कुछ करने से पहले दूसरी line underline कीजिए. Blood glucose normal है. इतने छोटे सवाल में normal value कभी सजावट नहीं होती. वही discriminator है।
Diagram दोनों tests दिखा रहा है. बायाँ panel: glucose value क्या rule out करती है. दायाँ panel: असल में खो क्या रहा है. इसी क्रम में चलिए।
पहला step. Diabetes नाम वाले दो अलग disorders हैं, और urine ज़्यादा जाने के अलावा उनमें कुछ भी common नहीं. आगे बढ़ने से पहले इन्हें अलग कीजिए।
दूसरा step. Diabetes mellitus insulin की problem है, और उसमें blood glucose high होना चाहिए, glycosuria के साथ, प्यास और बार-बार urination भी. यहाँ glucose normal है, तो mellitus rule out।
तीसरा step. पूछिए कि body से निकल क्या रहा है. Urine dilute है, यानी ज़्यादातर पानी. Patient पानी खो रहा है, चीनी नहीं. इससे पूरा सवाल water handling पर आ जाता है।
पानी को कौन handle करता है? A D H kidney से water reabsorption कराता है. उसे हटा दीजिए तो kidney पानी वापस खींच ही नहीं पाएगी, और बहुत सारा dilute urine बाहर जाएगा, और प्यास उसी loss के पीछे आती है।
तो जवाब है A D H deficiency, यानी diabetes insipidus, और source है posterior pituitary. ध्यान दीजिए, सारा काम उस normal glucose ने किया. जो value boring लगे, उसे पढ़िए।

sections.title: Pitfalls: the pituitary traps that decide the mark

board_events.text: Pituitary: the traps
The posterior pituitary MAKES nothing. Oxytocin and ADH are hypothalamic in origin.
Trap: treating 'GH excess' as one disorder. Childhood gives gigantism; adulthood gives acromegaly.
Trap: putting MSH inside FLAT PiG. MSH comes from the pars intermedia.
Trap: diabetes insipidus is an ADH problem. Diabetes mellitus is an insulin problem.
Two routes, never mixed: portal BLOOD to the anterior lobe, NERVE FIBRES to the posterior lobe.
Releasing hormone switches on, inhibiting hormone switches off. Somatostatin inhibits GH.
All pituitary hormones are proteins or peptides, which fixes their mechanism of action later.

segments.text: The pituitary is dense, so the traps are dense too. These eight lines are where the marks actually move.

The biggest one first. The posterior pituitary makes nothing. If a question asks which hormones the posterior pituitary secretes, the honest answer is that it releases oxytocin and A D H, but both are hypothalamic in origin.
Second: do not treat growth hormone excess as one disorder. Childhood excess is gigantism, adult excess is acromegaly. A question that mentions an age is telling you which one it wants.
Third: M S H is not part of FLAT PiG. It comes from the pars intermedia and acts on melanocytes for skin pigmentation. Adding it to the six is a classic overreach.

Fourth, and the one that costs the most: the two diabetes. Insipidus is an A D H problem with normal glucose. Mellitus is an insulin problem with high glucose. Same word, different gland, different chapter section.
Fifth: never mix the two routes. Portal blood link goes to the anterior lobe. Nerve fibres go to the posterior lobe. If you can say that sentence, half this subtopic is secure.
Sixth: keep the switch language straight. A releasing hormone switches an anterior-pituitary hormone on. An inhibiting hormone switches it off. G n R H releases, somatostatin inhibits growth hormone.

And carry this one forward deliberately. Every pituitary hormone is a protein or peptide. When we reach mechanism of hormone action, that single fact will tell you which receptor they use before you think about it.
Pituitary dense है, तो traps भी dense हैं. ये आठ lines ही असल में marks हिलाती हैं।

सबसे बड़ा पहले. Posterior pituitary कुछ बनाता नहीं. अगर सवाल पूछे कि posterior pituitary कौन से hormones secrete करता है, तो सही जवाब है कि वो oxytocin और A D H release करता है, पर दोनों का origin hypothalamus है।
दूसरा: growth hormone के excess को एक disorder मत मानिए. बचपन का excess gigantism है, adult का excess acromegaly. सवाल में उम्र का ज़िक्र है, तो वही बता रहा है कि कौन सा चाहिए।
तीसरा: M S H, FLAT PiG का हिस्सा नहीं है. वो pars intermedia से आता है और melanocytes पर skin pigmentation के लिए act करता है. उसे छह में जोड़ना classic overreach है।
चौथा, और सबसे महँगा: दो diabetes. Insipidus, A D H की problem, glucose normal. Mellitus, insulin की problem, glucose high. एक ही शब्द, अलग gland, chapter का अलग हिस्सा।
पाँचवाँ: दोनों routes कभी मत मिलाइए. Portal blood link anterior lobe तक. Nerve fibres posterior lobe तक. यह एक line बोल पाए तो आधा subtopic पक्का।
छठा: switch वाली भाषा साफ रखिए. Releasing hormone anterior-pituitary hormone को ON करता है. Inhibiting hormone उसे OFF करता है. G n R H release कराता है, somatostatin growth hormone को रोकता है।
और यह जान-बूझकर आगे ले जाइए. हर pituitary hormone protein या peptide है. जब mechanism of hormone action पर पहुँचेंगे, तो यही एक fact सोचने से पहले बता देगा कि इनका receptor कौन सा है।

board_events.text: Core job: melatonin regulates the 24-hour, or diurnal, rhythm of the body.
That means the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature.
It also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle, and defence or immune capability.
Sometimes called the anti-ageing hormone.

segments.text: The pineal gland is small, it is quick to learn, and it is very reliably asked. So learn it properly once and it is yours.
Location first, because that is a one-mark question by itself. The pineal gland sits on the dorsal side of the forebrain.
And it secretes melatonin. One gland, one hormone to remember. This is the simplest entry in the whole chapter.
Think of it as the body's internal clock, as the picture shows. Day and night cues come in, and timing signals for rhythmic functions go out.

The core job: melatonin regulates the twenty four hour rhythm of the body, which is called the diurnal rhythm. If a question mentions rhythm or a daily cycle, your hand should already be moving toward melatonin.
What sits inside that rhythm? The sleep-wake cycle, and body temperature. Both of them rise and fall on a daily loop, and both are timed here.
Melatonin also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle, and defence or immune capability. That is a wider reach than students expect, and each of those has shown up as an option.
<curious>And one more label to carry: melatonin is sometimes called the anti-ageing hormone. It sounds like a slogan, but it is in your source, so it can be asked.
Pineal gland छोटी है, जल्दी सीख जाती है, और बहुत भरोसे से पूछी जाती है. तो एक बार ठीक से सीख लीजिए, फिर यह आपकी है।
पहले location, क्योंकि यह अकेले में एक मार्क का सवाल है. Pineal gland forebrain के dorsal side पर बैठी है।
और यह melatonin secrete करती है. एक gland, एक hormone. पूरे chapter की सबसे simple entry यही है।
इसे body की internal clock समझिए, जैसा तस्वीर में है. दिन-रात के cues अंदर आते हैं, और rhythmic functions के लिए timing signals बाहर जाते हैं।
मुख्य काम: melatonin body की चौबीस घंटे वाली rhythm regulate करता है, जिसे diurnal rhythm कहते हैं. सवाल में rhythm या daily cycle दिखे, तो हाथ अपने आप melatonin की तरफ जाना चाहिए।
उस rhythm के अंदर क्या आता है? Sleep-wake cycle, और body temperature. दोनों रोज़ एक loop में ऊपर-नीचे होते हैं, और दोनों की timing यहीं से होती है।
Melatonin metabolism, pigmentation, menstrual cycle, और defence यानी immune capability को भी influence करता है. यह reach students की उम्मीद से ज़्यादा है, और इनमें से हर एक option बनकर आया है।
<curious>और एक label साथ रखिए: melatonin को कभी-कभी anti-ageing hormone कहा जाता है. सुनने में slogan लगता है, पर यह आपके source में है, तो पूछा जा सकता है।

board_events.text: Step 1: name what kind of complaint this is. It is a TIMING complaint, not an intensity complaint.
Step 2: the pineal gland secretes melatonin, which regulates the diurnal rhythm. That is a match.
Step 3: rule out the thyroid. T3 and T4 set the basal metabolic rate, not the clock.
Step 4: rule out the adrenal medulla. Adrenaline raises alertness in an emergency, not on a daily schedule.
Rule: match the TIME SCALE of the symptom to the hormone's job.

segments.text: Let us practise the reasoning move this subtopic really tests, because the pineal is almost never asked as pure recall. It is asked as a discrimination.
The case: a person's sleep-wake cycle keeps drifting out of phase with day and night. Name the gland and hormone, and be ready to say why not the others.
The picture shows the shape of the answer. One match on the left, and two tempting distractors that you must actively knock down.
Step one, and this is the real skill: name the kind of complaint. Nothing here is too strong or too weak. Something is happening at the wrong time. This is a timing complaint.
Step two: which hormone's job is timing? The pineal secretes melatonin, and melatonin regulates the diurnal rhythm, meaning the sleep-wake cycle and body temperature. Complaint and job match exactly.

Step three: rule out the thyroid deliberately. T three and T four set the basal metabolic rate. A thyroid patient can absolutely feel tired, but that is an intensity problem, a dial turned too far, not a clock running out of phase.

Step four: rule out the adrenal medulla. Adrenaline raises alertness, and yes, alertness is in the story. But adrenaline is an emergency hormone, fired for a crisis, not a hormone that keeps a daily schedule.

<whisper>So keep the rule, not just the answer. Match the time scale of the symptom to the time scale of the hormone's job. Daily rhythm goes to the clock, emergency goes to the medulla, ongoing rate goes to the thyroid.
अब वो reasoning move practise करते हैं जो यह subtopic असल में test करता है, क्योंकि pineal शायद ही कभी pure recall में पूछी जाती है. उसे discrimination की तरह पूछा जाता है।
Case: एक व्यक्ति का sleep-wake cycle दिन-रात से बार-बार out of phase हो जाता है. Gland और hormone बताइए, और यह भी कि बाकी क्यों नहीं।
तस्वीर जवाब का shape दिखा रही है. बाईं तरफ एक match, और दो tempting distractors जिन्हें आपको खुद गिराना है।
पहला step, और असली skill यही है: complaint का type पहचानिए. यहाँ कुछ भी ज़्यादा तेज़ या ज़्यादा धीमा नहीं है. कुछ गलत वक्त पर हो रहा है. यह timing की complaint है।
दूसरा step: timing किसका काम है? Pineal melatonin secrete करती है, और melatonin diurnal rhythm regulate करता है, यानी sleep-wake cycle और body temperature. Complaint और job बिलकुल match।

तीसरा step: thyroid को जान-बूझकर rule out कीजिए. T three और T four basal metabolic rate set करते हैं. Thyroid का patient थकान महसूस कर सकता है, पर वो intensity की problem है, dial ज़्यादा घूम गया, clock out of phase नहीं हुआ।
चौथा step: adrenal medulla rule out कीजिए. Adrenaline alertness बढ़ाता है, और हाँ, कहानी में alertness है भी. पर adrenaline emergency hormone है, crisis में चलता है, रोज़ का schedule नहीं रखता।
<whisper>तो सिर्फ जवाब नहीं, rule याद रखिए. Symptom के time scale को hormone के काम के time scale से match कीजिए. Daily rhythm clock को, emergency medulla को, ongoing rate thyroid को।

sections.title: Pitfalls: the pineal traps

board_events.text: Pineal: small gland, sharp traps
Trap: melatonin and melanin are different words. Melatonin is the pineal clock hormone.
MSH from the pars intermedia acts on melanocytes for pigmentation. Do not swap it with melatonin.
Trap: naming the wrong position. The pineal is on the DORSAL side of the forebrain.
Trap: shrinking melatonin to sleep only. It also covers body temperature within the diurnal rhythm.
Its wider influence: metabolism, pigmentation, menstrual cycle, defence and immunity.
Diurnal means the 24-hour day-night cycle. That word is the giveaway in a question stem.
The pineal has no classical excess or deficiency disorder in this chapter's table. Do not invent one.

segments.text: The pineal is small, but it has traps out of all proportion to its size, and almost all of them are about words.
The first trap is pure vocabulary. Melatonin and melanin are not the same word. Melatonin is the pineal hormone, and it is a clock hormone. Read the option twice before you tick it.

The related confusion: M S H, from the pars intermedia, acts on melanocytes to control pigmentation. That is the pigment hormone. Melatonin does influence pigmentation, but its core job is the rhythm.

Second trap: position. The pineal gland is on the dorsal side of the forebrain. Dorsal is the word. If an option says ventral, or puts it at the base of the brain, that is the pituitary's address, not this one.
Third trap: shrinking melatonin down to sleep. The diurnal rhythm it regulates includes body temperature as well as the sleep-wake cycle. Both belong in a full-mark answer.
Fourth: the wider list. Metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle, and defence or immune capability. Students who only memorise sleep get caught by exactly these options.
Fifth, a keyword habit. Diurnal means the twenty four hour day-night cycle. When that word appears in a stem, it is pointing straight at melatonin. Treat it as a signpost.
And a discipline point. In this chapter's table, the pineal has no classical excess or deficiency disorder listed. If an option offers you an invented pineal disease, that is the distractor.
Pineal छोटी है, पर उसके traps उसके size से कहीं बड़े हैं, और लगभग सारे शब्दों के हैं।
पहला trap शुद्ध vocabulary का है. Melatonin और melanin एक शब्द नहीं हैं. Melatonin pineal का hormone है, और वो clock hormone है. Option पर tick करने से पहले दो बार पढ़िए।

इससे जुड़ा confusion: M S H, pars intermedia से, melanocytes पर act करके pigmentation control करता है. वो pigment वाला hormone है. Melatonin pigmentation को influence करता ज़रूर है, पर उसका core job rhythm है।
दूसरा trap: position. Pineal gland forebrain के dorsal side पर है. शब्द है dorsal. कोई option ventral कहे, या brain के base पर बताए, तो वो पता pituitary का है, इसका नहीं।
तीसरा trap: melatonin को सिर्फ नींद तक सीमित कर देना. जिस diurnal rhythm को वो regulate करता है उसमें body temperature भी है और sleep-wake cycle भी. पूरे मार्क के जवाब में दोनों चाहिए।
चौथा: बड़ी list. Metabolism, pigmentation, menstrual cycle, और defence यानी immune capability. जो students सिर्फ sleep रटते हैं, वो ठीक इन्हीं options में फँसते हैं।
पाँचवाँ, एक keyword आदत. Diurnal यानी चौबीस घंटे का day-night cycle. यह शब्द stem में दिखे तो वो सीधे melatonin की तरफ इशारा है. इसे signpost मानिए।
और एक discipline की बात. इस chapter की table में pineal के लिए कोई classical excess या deficiency disorder नहीं है. कोई option आपको बना-बनाया pineal disease दे, तो वही distractor है।

board_events.text: FOLLICULAR cells make T4 (thyroxine) and T3 (triiodothyronine), from tyrosine plus iodine.
T3 and T4 set the basal metabolic rate, and control carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism.
They also support RBC formation and maintain water and electrolyte balance.
PARAFOLLICULAR, or C, cells make thyrocalcitonin, also written TCT or calcitonin.
Calcitonin is a NON-iodinated protein hormone. It lowers blood calcium: hypocalcemic.

segments.text: The thyroid is the largest endocrine gland in the body, and it is the one gland students most often reduce to a single job. It actually runs two, and they have nothing to do with each other.
Anatomy first. Two lobes flanking the trachea in the neck. And one fact that explains half its disorders: the thyroid holds the body's largest iodine reserve.
Now the split that matters. Look at the two panels. One gland, two different cell types, two completely different hormones. Almost every thyroid trap lives in the gap between these panels.
Follicular cells make T four, thyroxine, and T three, triiodothyronine. And note what they are built from: tyrosine plus iodine. That is why an iodine shortage becomes a thyroid disease.

What do T three and T four do? They set the basal metabolic rate, the body's baseline burn. And they control carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism. This is the gland that decides your body's running speed.
They do two more things students forget: they support R B C formation, and they maintain water and electrolyte balance. Both appear as options, and both are correct.
Now the second cell type. Parafollicular cells, also called C cells, make thyrocalcitonin, which you will see written as T C T or simply calcitonin.

<excited>And here is the surprise. Calcitonin is a non-iodinated protein hormone, and its job is to lower blood calcium. It is hypocalcemic. It has nothing to do with metabolism, no iodine in it, and it lives in the same gland.
Thyroid body की सबसे बड़ी endocrine gland है, और यही वो gland है जिसे students सबसे ज़्यादा एक ही काम तक सीमित कर देते हैं. असल में यह दो काम चलाती है, और उन दोनों का आपस में कोई रिश्ता नहीं।
पहले anatomy. गर्दन में trachea के दोनों तरफ दो lobes. और एक fact जो इसके आधे disorders समझा देता है: body का सबसे बड़ा iodine reserve thyroid में है।
अब वो split जो मायने रखता है. दोनों panels देखिए. एक gland, दो अलग cell types, दो बिलकुल अलग hormones. Thyroid के लगभग सारे traps इन्हीं दोनों के बीच की खाई में हैं।
Follicular cells बनाते हैं T four यानी thyroxine, और T three यानी triiodothyronine. और ध्यान दीजिए ये बनते किससे हैं: tyrosine plus iodine. इसीलिए iodine की कमी thyroid की बीमारी बन जाती है।

T three और T four करते क्या हैं? वो basal metabolic rate set करते हैं, यानी body की baseline burn. और carbohydrate, protein, fat metabolism control करते हैं. यही gland तय करती है कि आपकी body किस speed पर चल रही है।
दो काम और, जो students भूल जाते हैं: वो R B C formation को support करते हैं, और water तथा electrolyte balance बनाए रखते हैं. दोनों options में आते हैं, और दोनों सही हैं।
अब दूसरा cell type. Parafollicular cells, जिन्हें C cells भी कहते हैं, thyrocalcitonin बनाते हैं, जिसे आप T C T या सिर्फ calcitonin लिखा देखेंगे।

<excited>और यहाँ surprise है. Calcitonin एक non-iodinated protein hormone है, और उसका काम है blood calcium घटाना. वो hypocalcemic है. उसका metabolism से कोई लेना-देना नहीं, उसमें iodine नहीं, और वो रहता उसी gland में है।

board_events.text: Iodine deficiency gives GOITRE, with hypothyroidism. T3 and T4 need iodine to be built.
Hypothyroidism in the foetus or infancy gives CRETINISM.
Cretinism: stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, deaf-mutism.
Hypothyroidism in adults gives MYXOEDEMA, also called Gull's disease.
Hyperthyroidism gives GRAVE'S DISEASE: exophthalmos and raised metabolism. It can also raise RBC count, called polycythemia.
The metabolic dial: too slow or too fast. The AGE then names the slow disorder.

segments.text: Thyroid disorders look like a list of names to memorise. They are not. They are one dial, and every name on the board is just a position on it.
Look at the two columns. Left, the dial turned down, hypothyroidism. Right, the dial turned up, hyperthyroidism. Sort any name into a column first, then recall the details.

Start with iodine, because it connects straight to the last section. T three and T four are built from tyrosine plus iodine. Take away the iodine and the gland cannot build them, so you get goitre along with hypothyroidism.
Now the slow column splits by age, exactly like growth hormone did. Hypothyroidism in the foetus or in infancy gives cretinism.
And cretinism is not vague. It is stunted growth, mental retardation, low I Q, and deaf-mutism. A developing body and a developing brain both needed that metabolic drive, and neither got it.
The same deficiency in an adult gives myxoedema, also called Gull's disease. The adult is already built, so what shows up is a sluggish metabolism and puffy skin rather than a failure to develop.
Now the fast column. Hyperthyroidism gives Grave's disease: exophthalmos, meaning protruding eyeballs, with raised metabolism. It can also raise the R B C count, which is called polycythemia.
<whisper>Hold the two-step. First, is the dial slow or fast? Then, if it is slow, at what age? Those two questions name every disorder on this board without memorising a list.
Thyroid disorders नामों की list जैसे लगते हैं. हैं नहीं. यह एक dial है, और board का हर नाम उसी dial की एक position है।
दोनों columns देखिए. बायाँ, dial नीचे, hypothyroidism. दायाँ, dial ऊपर, hyperthyroidism. पहले किसी भी नाम को column में डालिए, फिर details याद कीजिए।

Iodine से शुरू कीजिए, क्योंकि यह सीधे पिछले section से जुड़ता है. T three और T four tyrosine plus iodine से बनते हैं. Iodine हटा दीजिए तो gland इन्हें बना ही नहीं पाएगी, और goitre के साथ hypothyroidism मिलेगा।
अब slow column उम्र से बँटता है, बिलकुल growth hormone की तरह. Foetus या infancy में hypothyroidism देता है cretinism।
और cretinism अस्पष्ट नहीं है. उसमें है stunted growth, mental retardation, कम I Q, और deaf-mutism. विकसित होती body और विकसित होते brain, दोनों को वो metabolic drive चाहिए था, और किसी को मिला नहीं।
वही deficiency adult में देती है myxoedema, जिसे Gull's disease भी कहते हैं. Adult तो बन चुका है, इसलिए दिखता है sluggish metabolism और puffy skin, न कि विकास का रुक जाना।
अब fast column. Hyperthyroidism देता है Grave's disease: exophthalmos यानी बाहर निकली आँखें, और बढ़ा हुआ metabolism. यह R B C count भी बढ़ा सकता है, जिसे polycythemia कहते हैं।
<whisper>यह दो-step पकड़िए. पहले, dial slow है या fast? फिर, अगर slow है तो किस उम्र में? यही दो सवाल इस board के हर disorder का नाम बता देते हैं, बिना list रटे।

board_events.text: Step 1: both pictures are 'too slow'. That points to the thyroid, hormone thyroxine, T3 and T4.
Step 2: the child's picture is a FAILURE TO DEVELOP. That is CRETINISM.
Step 3: the adult's picture is a slowed but built body. That is MYXOEDEMA.
Same deficiency, different age sensitivity. The age is the discriminator, not the hormone.

segments.text: This one is from C B S E, and it is the cleanest test of the pattern we have just built. Two patients, and you must name one gland, one hormone, and two disorders.
The case: a child has stunted growth and low I Q. An adult with the same deficiency has puffy skin and a sluggish metabolism.
The question asks for the gland, the hormone, and both disorders. Notice the phrase same deficiency. The question has already told you it is one hormone, so do not go looking for two.
The diagram is the whole answer in one shape: a single deficiency at the top, and the branch below it labelled not by hormone but by age.
Step one. Both pictures read as too slow. Stunted, sluggish, low output. That is the metabolic dial turned down, so it is the thyroid, and the hormone is thyroxine, T three and T four.

Step two. Read the child's picture carefully. Stunted growth and low I Q is a failure to develop. A body and a brain that needed metabolic drive during construction and never received it. That is cretinism.
Step three. The adult's picture is different in kind. This body is already built, so nothing fails to develop. It just runs slow: puffy skin, sluggish metabolism. That is myxoedema.

So the answer: thyroid, thyroxine, child equals cretinism, adult equals myxoedema. Same deficiency, different age sensitivity. And that is the second time in this part that age, not hormone, has been the discriminator.
यह C B S E से है, और अभी जो pattern बनाया उसका सबसे साफ test यही है. दो patients, और आपको एक gland, एक hormone, और दो disorders बताने हैं।
Case: एक बच्चे में stunted growth और कम I Q है. उसी deficiency वाले adult में puffy skin और sluggish metabolism है।
सवाल gland, hormone, और दोनों disorders माँगता है. Same deficiency शब्द पर ध्यान दीजिए. सवाल पहले ही बता चुका है कि hormone एक ही है, तो दो मत खोजिए।
Diagram पूरा जवाब एक shape में दे रहा है: ऊपर एक deficiency, और नीचे वाली branch hormone से नहीं, उम्र से labelled है।
पहला step. दोनों तस्वीरें too slow पढ़ी जाती हैं. Stunted, sluggish, कम output. यह metabolic dial नीचे है, तो gland है thyroid, और hormone है thyroxine, यानी T three और T four।
दूसरा step. बच्चे की तस्वीर ध्यान से पढ़िए. Stunted growth और कम I Q, यानी विकास का ही न होना. एक body और एक brain जिन्हें बनते वक्त metabolic drive चाहिए था और मिला नहीं. यह cretinism है।
तीसरा step. Adult की तस्वीर तरह से ही अलग है. यह body बन चुकी है, तो विकास रुकने का सवाल नहीं. वो बस धीरे चल रही है: puffy skin, sluggish metabolism. यह myxoedema है।
तो जवाब: thyroid, thyroxine, बच्चा यानी cretinism, adult यानी myxoedema. वही deficiency, अलग age sensitivity. और इस part में यह दूसरी बार है जब उम्र, hormone नहीं, discriminator बनी है।

sections.title: Pitfalls: the thyroid traps

board_events.text: Thyroid: the traps
Trap: assuming everything from the thyroid needs iodine. Calcitonin is NON-iodinated.
Calcitonin comes from the thyroid, but PTH comes from the parathyroid. Different glands, opposite actions.
Trap: cretinism versus myxoedema. Both are hypothyroid. The age of onset separates them.
Goitre is caused by iodine deficiency and comes with hypothyroidism. Grave's disease is the opposite direction.
Grave's disease brings exophthalmos, protruding eyeballs, and can raise RBC count: polycythemia.
Myxoedema has a second name, Gull's disease. It is asked by either name.
Remember the quiet duties of T3 and T4: RBC formation, and water and electrolyte balance.

segments.text: The thyroid gives up more marks than any other gland in this chapter, mostly to five specific traps. Here they are.
First and biggest: assuming everything from the thyroid needs iodine. Thyroxine does. Calcitonin does not. Calcitonin is explicitly a non-iodinated protein hormone from the same gland.
Second: calcitonin is from the thyroid, but P T H is from the parathyroid. Two different glands with opposite actions on calcium. The names sound related, the sources are not.
Third: cretinism versus myxoedema. Both are hypothyroidism. Do not treat them as different hormone problems. The age of onset separates them, and nothing else.

Fourth, a direction trap. Goitre comes from iodine deficiency and travels with hypothyroidism. Grave's disease is hyperthyroidism, the opposite direction. Both involve the thyroid; they point opposite ways.

Fifth: know Grave's by its markers. Exophthalmos, the protruding eyeballs, and raised metabolism, and it can raise the R B C count, which is polycythemia. That eyeball sign is the single strongest giveaway in a stem.
A naming point that catches people: myxoedema is also called Gull's disease. The paper may use either name and expects you to answer the same way.

And finally, do not lose the quiet duties. T three and T four also support R B C formation and maintain water and electrolyte balance. Students who only say B M R miss the option that was actually correct.
इस chapter में सबसे ज़्यादा marks thyroid ही देती है, और ज़्यादातर पाँच खास traps को. ये रहे।
पहला और सबसे बड़ा: यह मान लेना कि thyroid से निकलने वाली हर चीज़ को iodine चाहिए. Thyroxine को चाहिए. Calcitonin को नहीं. Calcitonin साफ तौर पर उसी gland का non-iodinated protein hormone है।
दूसरा: calcitonin thyroid से है, पर P T H parathyroid से. दो अलग glands, calcium पर उल्टे actions. नाम जुड़े हुए लगते हैं, sources नहीं हैं।
तीसरा: cretinism बनाम myxoedema. दोनों hypothyroidism हैं. इन्हें अलग hormone की problem मत समझिए. इन्हें सिर्फ onset की उम्र अलग करती है, और कुछ नहीं।
चौथा, direction वाला trap. Goitre iodine deficiency से आता है और hypothyroidism के साथ चलता है. Grave's disease hyperthyroidism है, उल्टी दिशा. दोनों में thyroid है; दिशाएँ उल्टी हैं।

पाँचवाँ: Grave's को उसके markers से पहचानिए. Exophthalmos यानी बाहर निकली आँखें, बढ़ा हुआ metabolism, और R B C count बढ़ सकता है, जिसे polycythemia कहते हैं. Stem में वो आँख वाला sign सबसे तगड़ा इशारा है।
एक naming point जो लोगों को फँसाता है: myxoedema को Gull's disease भी कहते हैं. Paper कोई भी नाम इस्तेमाल कर सकता है और जवाब वही चाहिए।

और आखिर में, वो चुपचाप वाले काम मत छोड़िए. T three और T four, R B C formation को support करते हैं और water तथा electrolyte balance रखते हैं. जो students सिर्फ B M R कहते हैं, वो अक्सर सही option ही छोड़ आते हैं।

board_events.text: Parathyroid: four glands, one job
Four glands embedded on the back of the thyroid. A different gland, sitting on the thyroid.
PTH, the parathyroid hormone, also called Collip's hormone. It is a peptide.

board_events.text: PTH RAISES blood calcium. It is hypercalcemic.
It does this three ways: bone resorption, calcium reabsorption in the kidney, and calcium absorption from the gut.
PTH and calcitonin are ANTAGONISTS. This is the calcium see-saw.
PTH deficiency gives tetany, low-calcium muscle spasms. Excess gives osteitis fibrosa, bone weakening.

segments.text: The parathyroids are four small glands embedded on the back of the thyroid. Sitting on the thyroid, but not part of it. That physical arrangement is the source of nearly every confusion here.
Say it once, clearly: a different gland, in a different chapter row, with a different hormone, that happens to sit on the thyroid's back surface.
The hormone is P T H, parathyroid hormone, which your source also calls Collip's hormone. It is a peptide. Note that, because peptide will decide its mechanism later.
Now the see-saw, and this is the picture to carry out of this section. P T H on one side pushing calcium up. Calcitonin from the thyroid's C cells on the other side pulling it down.
P T H raises blood calcium. It is hypercalcemic. If you remember one word for this gland, it is up.

It raises calcium through three routes, and you should be able to list all three. Bone resorption, dissolving calcium out of bone. Calcium reabsorption in the kidney, keeping it from being lost. And calcium absorption from the gut, bringing more in.
<excited>P T H and calcitonin are antagonists. This is the calcium see-saw, and it is the most reliably asked antagonistic pair in the chapter after insulin and glucagon.

And the failures sit on either end. P T H deficiency means calcium stays low, giving tetany, which is low-calcium muscle spasms. Excess means bone is stripped too hard, giving osteitis fibrosa, bone weakening.
Parathyroids चार छोटी glands हैं जो thyroid के पीछे embedded हैं. Thyroid पर बैठी हुई, पर उसका हिस्सा नहीं. यही physical arrangement यहाँ की लगभग हर confusion की जड़ है।
एक बार साफ बोलिए: यह अलग gland है, chapter की अलग row में, अलग hormone के साथ, जो बस thyroid की पिछली सतह पर बैठी है।
Hormone है P T H, parathyroid hormone, जिसे आपका source Collip's hormone भी कहता है. यह एक peptide है. ध्यान रखिए, क्योंकि peptide होना आगे इसका mechanism तय करेगा।
अब see-saw, और इस section से यही तस्वीर साथ ले जानी है. एक तरफ P T H calcium ऊपर धकेलता हुआ. दूसरी तरफ thyroid के C cells से calcitonin उसे नीचे खींचता हुआ।
P T H blood calcium बढ़ाता है. वो hypercalcemic है. इस gland के लिए एक शब्द याद रखना हो, तो वो है ऊपर।

यह calcium तीन रास्तों से बढ़ाता है, और तीनों बोल पाने चाहिए. Bone resorption, यानी हड्डी से calcium घोलकर निकालना. Kidney में calcium reabsorption, यानी उसे बाहर जाने से रोकना. और gut से calcium absorption, यानी और अंदर लाना।
<excited>P T H और calcitonin antagonists हैं. यही calcium see-saw है, और insulin-glucagon के बाद chapter की सबसे भरोसे से पूछी जाने वाली antagonistic pair यही है।

और failures दोनों सिरों पर बैठी हैं. P T H की deficiency यानी calcium नीचे ही रह गया, तो tetany, यानी low-calcium muscle spasms. Excess यानी हड्डी से ज़्यादा खिंच गया, तो osteitis fibrosa, यानी bone weakening।

segments.text: Now let us use the see-saw as a reasoning tool rather than a picture to memorise. A patient has painful muscle spasms, and blood calcium is low.
One more line of history: there was surgery in the neck region. In an assertion-style question, a detail like that is placed there on purpose. Neck means thyroid and parathyroid territory.
The diagram walks the three steps. Read it left to right, and notice that the answer is reached by asking which side failed, not by recalling a disease name.
Step one. Calcium is low. On a see-saw, one end goes down either because that end lost its push, or because the other end pushed harder. Ask which one first.
The default reading is the raiser has failed. If the hormone that pushes calcium up stops arriving, calcium simply falls. That is the simpler and far more common explanation.

Step two. Who is the raiser? P T H, from the four parathyroid glands embedded on the back of the thyroid. And now the neck surgery detail pays off, because those glands sit exactly where the surgery was.
Step three. Low calcium from lost P T H gives tetany, which your source defines precisely as low-calcium muscle spasms. Symptom, mechanism and name now all line up.

<whisper>And keep the trap in view. Calcitonin excess would also lower calcium, so it is not a wrong idea. But the surgical clue sits on the parathyroids, so read the raiser first. In a see-saw question, always ask which side lost its push.
अब see-saw को रटी हुई तस्वीर नहीं, reasoning tool की तरह इस्तेमाल करते हैं. एक patient को दर्दनाक muscle spasms हैं, और blood calcium कम है।
History की एक और line: गर्दन के हिस्से में surgery हुई थी. ऐसे सवाल में यह detail जान-बूझकर रखी जाती है. गर्दन यानी thyroid और parathyroid का इलाका।
Diagram तीनों steps चलाता है. बाएँ से दाएँ पढ़िए, और देखिए कि जवाब disease का नाम याद करके नहीं, यह पूछकर मिलता है कि fail किस तरफ हुआ।
पहला step. Calcium कम है. See-saw पर एक सिरा या तो इसलिए गिरता है कि उसने धक्का देना बंद कर दिया, या इसलिए कि दूसरे सिरे ने ज़्यादा दबाया. पहले यही पूछिए।
Default पढ़ाई यह है कि raiser fail हुआ है. अगर calcium को ऊपर धकेलने वाला hormone आना ही बंद कर दे, तो calcium गिर जाएगा. यही simpler और कहीं ज़्यादा common explanation है।
दूसरा step. Raiser कौन है? P T H, thyroid के पीछे embedded चार parathyroid glands से. और अब neck surgery वाली detail काम आती है, क्योंकि वो glands ठीक वहीं बैठी हैं जहाँ surgery हुई।
तीसरा step. P T H जाने से calcium कम, और उससे tetany, जिसे आपका source ठीक इन्हीं शब्दों में low-calcium muscle spasms कहता है. Symptom, mechanism और नाम, तीनों अब एक line में हैं।

<whisper>और trap को नज़र में रखिए. Calcitonin की excess भी calcium घटाएगी, तो वो सोच गलत नहीं है. पर surgical clue parathyroids पर बैठा है, इसलिए पहले raiser पढ़िए. See-saw वाले सवाल में हमेशा पूछिए कि धक्का किस तरफ से छूटा।

sections.title: Pitfalls: the parathyroid and calcium traps

board_events.text: Parathyroid: the traps
Trap: 'on the thyroid' does not mean 'part of the thyroid'. Four separate glands, on its back.
PTH raises calcium. Calcitonin lowers it. Do not let the shared syllables blur the direction.
Source check: PTH is from the parathyroid; calcitonin is from the thyroid's parafollicular C cells.
Trap: naming only one route. PTH acts on bone, kidney AND gut. All three earn the mark.
Deficiency gives tetany; excess gives osteitis fibrosa. Deficiency is the one that spasms.
PTH is also called Collip's hormone, and it is a peptide, not a steroid.
PTH and calcitonin are an antagonistic pair, alongside insulin and glucagon for blood glucose.

segments.text: The parathyroid is one paragraph of content and a surprising number of ways to lose the mark. Almost all of them are direction or source errors.
First: on the thyroid does not mean part of the thyroid. Four separate glands, embedded on its back surface. Different gland, different hormone, different row in the table.
Second, the direction. P T H raises calcium; calcitonin lowers it. The words share syllables and students blur them under time pressure. Fix them with the see-saw picture, not with the spelling.

Third, the source check, which is the assertion-reason favourite. P T H is from the parathyroid. Calcitonin is from the thyroid's parafollicular C cells. An option that swaps the sources is designed to look right.

Fourth: do not name only one route. P T H raises calcium by bone resorption, by calcium reabsorption in the kidney, and by calcium absorption from the gut. Three routes, and a three-mark answer wants all three.

Fifth, the disorders. Deficiency gives tetany, the low-calcium muscle spasms. Excess gives osteitis fibrosa, the bone weakening. If you can only hold one, hold this: deficiency is the one that spasms.
Sixth, the alternative names. P T H is also called Collip's hormone. And it is a peptide, not a steroid, which will matter when we reach mechanism of hormone action.

And carry the pairing out of this part. P T H and calcitonin are an antagonistic pair for blood calcium, sitting alongside insulin and glucagon for blood glucose. Antagonistic pairs are how this chapter keeps everything balanced, and we build that idea properly later.
Parathyroid पर content एक paragraph है, पर मार्क गँवाने के तरीके हैरान करने वाले हैं. लगभग सब direction या source की गलतियाँ हैं।
पहला: thyroid पर होना यह नहीं कि thyroid का हिस्सा है. उसकी पिछली सतह पर embedded चार अलग glands. अलग gland, अलग hormone, table की अलग row।

दूसरा, direction. P T H calcium बढ़ाता है; calcitonin घटाता है. शब्दों की आवाज़ मिलती-जुलती है और time pressure में students गड्ड-मड्ड कर देते हैं. इन्हें spelling से नहीं, see-saw की तस्वीर से पक्का कीजिए।

तीसरा, source check, जो assertion-reason का favourite है. P T H parathyroid से है. Calcitonin thyroid के parafollicular C cells से. जो option sources को आपस में बदल दे, वो सही दिखने के लिए ही बनाया गया है।
चौथा: सिर्फ एक route मत बताइए. P T H calcium बढ़ाता है bone resorption से, kidney में calcium reabsorption से, और gut से calcium absorption से. तीन routes, और तीन मार्क का जवाब तीनों माँगता है।
पाँचवाँ, disorders. Deficiency देती है tetany, यानी low-calcium muscle spasms. Excess देती है osteitis fibrosa, यानी bone weakening. एक ही याद रख पाएँ तो यह रखिए: spasms deficiency वाली तरफ हैं।
छठा, दूसरे नाम. P T H को Collip's hormone भी कहते हैं. और वो peptide है, steroid नहीं, जो mechanism of hormone action पर मायने रखेगा।

और यह जोड़ी इस part से साथ ले जाइए. P T H और calcitonin blood calcium की antagonistic pair हैं, जैसे insulin और glucagon blood glucose की. यही antagonistic pairs इस chapter में सब कुछ balance में रखते हैं, और उस idea को हम आगे ठीक से बनाएँगे।

board_events.text: Its hormone is THYMOSIN.
Thymosin drives the differentiation of T-lymphocytes.
That gives cell-mediated immunity. It also supports antibody production.
The thymus DEGENERATES with age, weakening immunity in the elderly.
That degeneration is a normal part of ageing, not a disease.

segments.text: The thymus is short to learn and quietly high-yield, because it is the one endocrine gland that talks to the immune system.
Position first. It is a lobular gland lying on the dorsal side of the heart, near the aorta. Dorsal side of the heart. That phrase is the whole location answer.
The picture holds three things, and they are the only three you need: where it sits, what it secretes, and the fact that it fades.
Its hormone is thymosin. One gland, one hormone. Like the pineal, this is a clean pairing with nothing to confuse.

Thymosin drives the differentiation of T lymphocytes. Not their birth, their differentiation. They arrive and the thymus turns them into working T cells. Think of it as the training school, not the maternity ward.
What does that buy the body? Cell-mediated immunity. And thymosin also supports antibody production, so it touches both arms of the immune response.
Now the fact that makes this gland unusual. The thymus degenerates with age, and immunity weakens in the elderly as a result. Your source says this plainly.
<curious>And note the careful wording, because this is exactly where a question can catch you. That degeneration is a normal part of ageing. It is not a disease, and it is not a disorder to be named.
Thymus सीखने में छोटी है और चुपचाप high-yield है, क्योंकि यही अकेली endocrine gland है जो immune system से बात करती है।
पहले position. यह एक lobular gland है जो heart के dorsal side पर, aorta के पास है. Heart का dorsal side. यही phrase पूरा location वाला जवाब है।
तस्वीर में तीन चीज़ें हैं, और यही तीन चाहिए: कहाँ है, क्या secrete करती है, और यह कि समय के साथ घट जाती है।
इसका hormone है thymosin. एक gland, एक hormone. Pineal की तरह यह भी साफ जोड़ी है, कोई confusion नहीं।

Thymosin, T lymphocytes का differentiation चलाता है. उनका जन्म नहीं, उनका differentiation. वो आते हैं और thymus उन्हें काम करने वाले T cells बना देती है. इसे training school समझिए, maternity ward नहीं।
इससे body को क्या मिलता है? Cell-mediated immunity. और thymosin antibody production को भी support करता है, यानी यह immune response की दोनों भुजाओं को छूता है।
अब वो fact जो इस gland को अलग बनाता है. Thymus उम्र के साथ degenerate होती है, और इसी वजह से बुज़ुर्गों में immunity कमज़ोर होती है. आपका source यह साफ कहता है।
<curious>और शब्दों पर ध्यान दीजिए, क्योंकि सवाल यहीं पकड़ता है. यह degeneration ageing का normal हिस्सा है. यह बीमारी नहीं है, और इसका कोई disorder नाम नहीं देना है।

board_events.text: Step 1: the clue names a job, so answer with the gland whose hormone has exactly that job.
Thymus, thymosin. That is the match.
Rule out bone marrow: it is where the cells are born, and it is not a hormone source in this chapter.
Rule out cortisol from the adrenal cortex: it is immune-SUPPRESSING, the opposite direction.
Two hormones can touch immunity. Read the DIRECTION: one builds it, one suppresses it.

segments.text: This one comes straight from your source's C U E T match-style example, and it is worth slowing down on, because matching questions are won by ruling out, not by recalling.
The clue you are handed is: differentiation of T lymphocytes. Four words, and they are a job description.
The picture shows the shape of every match question. One correct pairing, and distractors that are close enough to feel right for two seconds.
Step one, and this is the discipline. The clue names a job, so do not scan for a familiar word. Ask which hormone has exactly this job, and answer with the gland behind it.
Thymus, thymosin. Thymosin drives T lymphocyte differentiation and gives cell-mediated immunity. Clue and job match word for word, so this is the answer.

Now rule out the tempting ones on purpose. Bone marrow feels right because it is deeply involved with blood cells. But it is where cells are born, not where they are trained, and it is not a hormone source in this chapter's table.
Rule out cortisol from the adrenal cortex. It is genuinely an immune hormone, so it is a real distractor. But cortisol is immune-suppressing. It points the opposite way.
<whisper>And take the general rule with you. When two hormones both touch one system, the direction decides. One builds immunity, one suppresses it. Direction is what a good distractor hides.
यह सीधे आपके source के C U E T match-style example से है, और इस पर रुकना ज़रूरी है, क्योंकि matching के सवाल याद करने से नहीं, rule out करने से जीते जाते हैं।
आपको clue मिला है: differentiation of T lymphocytes. चार शब्द, और वो एक job description हैं।
तस्वीर हर match वाले सवाल का shape दिखा रही है. एक सही जोड़ी, और distractors जो दो सेकंड के लिए सही लगते हैं।
पहला step, और यही discipline है. Clue एक job बता रहा है, तो जाना-पहचाना शब्द मत खोजिए. पूछिए कि यह job किस hormone का है, और उसके पीछे वाली gland बताइए।
Thymus, thymosin. Thymosin, T lymphocyte differentiation चलाता है और cell-mediated immunity देता है. Clue और job शब्द-दर-शब्द match हैं, तो यही जवाब है।

अब जान-बूझकर tempting वालों को rule out कीजिए. Bone marrow सही लगता है क्योंकि उसका blood cells से गहरा रिश्ता है. पर वो जन्म की जगह है, training की नहीं, और इस chapter की table में वो hormone source है ही नहीं।
Adrenal cortex का cortisol rule out कीजिए. वो सचमुच immune hormone है, इसलिए असली distractor है. पर cortisol immune-suppressing है. वो उल्टी दिशा में है।
<whisper>और general rule साथ ले जाइए. जब दो hormones एक ही system को छूते हों, तो direction फैसला करती है. एक immunity बनाता है, दूसरा दबाता है. अच्छा distractor यही direction छिपाता है।

sections.title: Pitfalls: the thymus traps

board_events.text: Thymus: the traps
Trap: calling age-related thymic degeneration a disease. It is normal ageing.
Thymosin drives T-lymphocyte DIFFERENTIATION. The marrow makes the cells; the thymus trains them.
Trap: thymosin and thyroxine are different hormones from different glands. Read the word fully.
Position: dorsal side of the heart, near the aorta. Not in the neck.
Thymosin gives cell-mediated immunity AND supports antibody production. Do not restrict it to T-cells alone.
Thymosin builds immunity; cortisol suppresses it. Opposite directions, and a favourite distractor pair.
The thymus has no excess or deficiency disorder named in this chapter's table.

segments.text: The thymus is one paragraph, so the traps are mostly about words and about what you must not invent.

The biggest one: do not call the thymus shrinking with age a disease. Your source calls it a normal part of ageing that weakens immunity in the elderly. If an option dresses it up as a disorder, that is the distractor.
Second: get the verb right. Thymosin drives the differentiation of T lymphocytes. The marrow makes the cells, the thymus trains them. Differentiation is the word that earns the mark.
Third, and this catches people under time pressure: thymosin and thyroxine start the same way and are completely different. Different gland, different job, no relationship. Read the whole word.
Fourth: position. Dorsal side of the heart, near the aorta. Not the neck. The neck is thyroid and parathyroid territory, and options love to move glands around.
Fifth: do not narrow it too far. Thymosin gives cell-mediated immunity and supports antibody production. Students who only say T-cells will reject a correct antibody option.
Sixth, the direction pair worth memorising as a pair: thymosin builds immunity, cortisol suppresses it. Both are real immune hormones. That is exactly why they appear together in options.
And the discipline point again. There is no thymic excess or deficiency disorder in this chapter's table. Do not invent one to fill a blank, because a blank is sometimes the correct answer.
Thymus एक paragraph की है, तो traps ज़्यादातर शब्दों के हैं और इस बात के कि आपको क्या नहीं गढ़ना है।

सबसे बड़ा: उम्र के साथ thymus का सिकुड़ना बीमारी मत कहिए. आपका source इसे ageing का normal हिस्सा कहता है जो बुज़ुर्गों में immunity कमज़ोर करता है. कोई option इसे disorder बनाकर पेश करे, तो वही distractor है।
दूसरा: verb सही रखिए. Thymosin, T lymphocytes का differentiation चलाता है. Marrow cells बनाता है, thymus उन्हें training देती है. Differentiation वही शब्द है जो मार्क दिलाता है।
तीसरा, और यह time pressure में पकड़ता है: thymosin और thyroxine शुरुआत में एक जैसे लगते हैं और पूरी तरह अलग हैं. अलग gland, अलग काम, कोई रिश्ता नहीं. पूरा शब्द पढ़िए।
चौथा: position. Heart का dorsal side, aorta के पास. गर्दन नहीं. गर्दन thyroid और parathyroid का इलाका है, और options को glands इधर-उधर करना बहुत पसंद है।
पाँचवाँ: दायरा छोटा मत कीजिए. Thymosin cell-mediated immunity देता है और antibody production को support करता है. जो students सिर्फ T-cells कहते हैं, वो सही antibody वाला option ठुकरा देते हैं।
छठा, वो direction वाली जोड़ी जिसे जोड़ी में ही याद रखिए: thymosin immunity बनाता है, cortisol उसे दबाता है. दोनों असली immune hormones हैं. इसीलिए options में साथ आते हैं।
और वही discipline वाली बात. इस chapter की table में thymus का कोई excess या deficiency disorder नहीं है. खाली जगह भरने के लिए कुछ गढ़िए मत, क्योंकि कभी-कभी खाली होना ही सही जवाब है।

board_events.text: MINERALOCORTICOIDS, mainly aldosterone: increase Na reabsorption and K excretion in the kidney.
They maintain fluid and electrolyte balance. Excess gives Conn's syndrome.
GLUCOCORTICOIDS, mainly cortisol: gluconeogenesis, lipolysis, proteolysis.
Cortisol is also anti-inflammatory and immune-suppressing, which is why it is used in organ transplants. Excess gives Cushing's syndrome.
SEX CORTICOIDS (androgens): excess gives adrenal virilism. Hypoactivity of the whole cortex gives Addison's disease.

segments.text: The adrenal glands sit one over each kidney, and each one is really two glands stacked together, with two completely different chemistries. We take the outer region first.

The cortex is the outer region, and it secretes steroid hormones called corticoids, arranged in three layers. Hold the word steroid, because at the end of this chapter it will decide their entire mechanism of action.
Look at the three bands. The layer names are not decoration. Each name states the job, which means you can reconstruct this whole board instead of memorising it.
First layer: mineralocorticoids, and the one to name is aldosterone. Mineral, meaning salt. It increases sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion in the kidney. Sodium in, potassium out.
That keeps fluid and electrolyte balance. And its excess has a name: Conn's syndrome. One layer, one disorder.
Second layer: glucocorticoids, and the one to name is cortisol. Gluco, meaning glucose. It drives gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, so it is breaking stores down to make fuel.
Cortisol has a second face that gets asked constantly: it is anti-inflammatory and immune-suppressing, which is exactly why it is used in organ transplants. And its excess is Cushing's syndrome.

<excited>Third layer: sex corticoids, the androgens, and their excess is adrenal virilism. And then one disorder that belongs to none of the layers: if the whole cortex is underactive, that is Addison's disease. Three excesses by layer, one deficiency for the lot.
Adrenal glands हर kidney के ऊपर एक-एक बैठी हैं, और असल में हर एक दो glands एक साथ हैं, दो बिलकुल अलग chemistries के साथ. पहले बाहरी हिस्सा लेते हैं।
Cortex बाहरी region है, और यह steroid hormones secrete करता है जिन्हें corticoids कहते हैं, तीन layers में. Steroid शब्द पकड़िए, क्योंकि chapter के आखिर में यही इनका पूरा mechanism तय करेगा।
तीनों bands देखिए. Layer के नाम सजावट नहीं हैं. हर नाम अपना काम बता रहा है, यानी आप इस पूरे board को रटने की जगह दोबारा बना सकते हैं।
पहली layer: mineralocorticoids, और नाम लेना है aldosterone का. Mineral यानी नमक. यह kidney में sodium reabsorption बढ़ाता है और potassium excretion बढ़ाता है. Sodium अंदर, potassium बाहर।
इससे fluid और electrolyte balance बना रहता है. और इसकी excess का नाम है Conn's syndrome. एक layer, एक disorder।
दूसरी layer: glucocorticoids, और नाम लेना है cortisol का. Gluco यानी glucose. यह gluconeogenesis, lipolysis और proteolysis चलाता है, यानी stores तोड़कर fuel बना रहा है।
Cortisol का दूसरा चेहरा लगातार पूछा जाता है: वो anti-inflammatory और immune-suppressing है, और ठीक इसीलिए organ transplants में इस्तेमाल होता है. और इसकी excess है Cushing's syndrome।

<excited>तीसरी layer: sex corticoids यानी androgens, और उनकी excess है adrenal virilism. और फिर एक disorder जो किसी layer का नहीं: अगर पूरा cortex कम काम करे, तो वो Addison's disease है. तीन excess layer से, और पूरे के लिए एक deficiency।
