segments.text: This case comes straight out of your source's feedback section, and it is the cleanest test of whether you understood the axis as a mechanism rather than a diagram.
The case: after the pituitary is removed, the adrenal cortex atrophies. Explain why. Work it by following the axis upward from the gland that failed.
Step one. Which axis is the adrenal cortex on? It runs on A C T H. That is the tropic hormone for this target gland, and it is the first thing to name.
Step two. Who makes A C T H? The anterior pituitary. And the anterior pituitary has just been removed. So the supply of A C T H has stopped completely.
Step three. With no tropic signal arriving at all, the cortex atrophies. And that word matters. It does not simply produce less. It physically wastes away.

So here is the principle the case is really teaching. A tropic hormone does not only trigger a gland. It maintains it. Constant stimulation is what keeps the target gland in working condition, so removing the signal removes the gland's upkeep.
Now the discriminator, which is where a harder version of this question goes. What happens to the adrenal medulla? It is in the same organ, so a careless answer says it atrophies too.

<whisper>But the medulla is not on this axis. It answers to nerves, not to A C T H. So the same operation does not waste it the same way. One organ, two regions, two completely different control systems. That is why the adrenal always gets two rows in the table, and this is the question that checks whether you knew why.
यह case सीधे आपके source के feedback वाले हिस्से से है, और यह सबसे साफ जाँच है कि आपने axis को diagram की तरह समझा या mechanism की तरह।
Case: pituitary हटाने के बाद adrenal cortex atrophy कर जाता है. कारण बताइए. इसे उस gland से शुरू करके axis के ऊपर की तरफ चलिए जो fail हुई।
पहला step. Adrenal cortex किस axis पर है? वो A C T H पर चलता है. इस target gland का tropic hormone यही है, और सबसे पहले इसी का नाम लेना है।
दूसरा step. A C T H कौन बनाता है? Anterior pituitary. और anterior pituitary अभी-अभी हटाया गया है. तो A C T H की सप्लाई पूरी तरह रुक गई।
तीसरा step. जब कोई tropic signal आ ही नहीं रहा, तो cortex atrophy कर जाता है. और यह शब्द मायने रखता है. वो सिर्फ कम नहीं बनाता. वो शारीरिक रूप से सूख जाता है।

तो यह case असल में जो principle सिखा रहा है वो यह है. Tropic hormone सिर्फ gland को चालू नहीं करता. वो उसे बनाए रखता है. लगातार stimulation ही target gland को काम लायक हालत में रखता है, तो signal हटाना gland की देखभाल हटा देना है।
अब discriminator, जहाँ इस सवाल का मुश्किल version जाता है. Adrenal medulla का क्या होगा? वो उसी organ में है, तो लापरवाह जवाब कहेगा कि वो भी atrophy करेगा।

<whisper>पर medulla इस axis पर है ही नहीं. वो nerves को जवाब देता है, A C T H को नहीं. तो वही operation उसे उस तरह नहीं सुखाता. एक organ, दो regions, दो बिलकुल अलग control systems. इसीलिए table में adrenal को हमेशा दो rows मिलती हैं, और यह सवाल जाँचता है कि आपको वजह पता थी या नहीं।

sections.title: Pitfalls: the feedback traps

board_events.text: Feedback: the traps
Negative feedback does not mean a bad effect. It means the product OPPOSES its own chain.
Rising T3 and T4 inhibit BOTH the pituitary and the hypothalamus. Not just the pituitary.
Trap: the adrenal medulla is not on a pituitary axis. It answers to nerves, not to a tropic hormone.
A tropic hormone maintains its target gland. Removing the pituitary atrophies the cortex.
Know the antagonistic pairs cold: insulin against glucagon, PTH against calcitonin, oxytocin against ADH.
Two designs, not one: the axes work by feedback down a chain; the pairs work by antagonism on one variable.
The unifying line: every command hormone is matched by a feedback or an antagonist signal.

segments.text: Feedback is the conceptual end of the chapter, so its traps are conceptual too. Get these right and the high-difficulty questions stop being frightening.

First, a word trap that costs marks every year. Negative feedback does not mean a harmful effect. Negative means opposing. The product opposes its own chain, and that is a stabilising thing, not a damaging one.
Second, a precision trap. Rising T three and T four inhibit both the pituitary and the hypothalamus. An option that says only the pituitary is incomplete, and incomplete is wrong.

Third, the one that separates strong students: the adrenal medulla is not on a pituitary axis. It answers to nerves. Every time a question puts the adrenal into a feedback chain, check whether it means cortex or medulla.
Fourth, the maintenance idea. A tropic hormone maintains its target gland; it does not merely trigger it. Removing the pituitary atrophies the cortex, and that fact is your evidence.
Fifth, know the antagonistic pairs cold, because they are the highest-frequency assertion-reason material in the chapter. Insulin against glucagon. P T H against calcitonin. Oxytocin against A D H.

Sixth, a conceptual distinction worth stating. There are two designs here, not one. The axes regulate by feedback down a hierarchy. The pairs regulate by antagonism on a single variable. Do not describe a see-saw as an axis.

And carry the unifying line out of the chapter, because it is a full-mark closing sentence for almost any long answer here. Every command hormone is matched by a feedback or an antagonist signal, keeping the internal environment stable.
Feedback chapter का conceptual सिरा है, तो इसके traps भी conceptual हैं. ये सही हो गए तो high-difficulty सवाल डराना बंद कर देंगे।

पहला, एक शब्द वाला trap जो हर साल marks काटता है. Negative feedback का मतलब नुकसान वाला असर नहीं. Negative यानी विरोधी. Product अपनी ही chain का विरोध करता है, और यह stabilise करने वाली बात है, नुकसान नहीं।
दूसरा, precision वाला trap. बढ़ते T three और T four, pituitary और hypothalamus दोनों को inhibit करते हैं. जो option सिर्फ pituitary कहे वो अधूरा है, और अधूरा गलत है।

तीसरा, वो जो अच्छे students को अलग करता है: adrenal medulla किसी pituitary axis पर नहीं है. वो nerves को जवाब देता है. जब भी सवाल adrenal को feedback chain में डाले, देखिए कि उसका मतलब cortex है या medulla।
चौथा, maintenance वाला idea. Tropic hormone अपनी target gland को बनाए रखता है; सिर्फ चालू नहीं करता. Pituitary हटाने से cortex atrophy करता है, और यही आपका सबूत है।
पाँचवाँ, antagonistic pairs पक्की कीजिए, क्योंकि chapter का सबसे ज़्यादा पूछा जाने वाला assertion-reason material यही है. Insulin बनाम glucagon. P T H बनाम calcitonin. Oxytocin बनाम A D H।
छठा, एक conceptual फर्क कहने लायक है. यहाँ दो designs हैं, एक नहीं. Axes hierarchy में feedback से regulate करते हैं. Pairs एक ही variable पर antagonism से. See-saw को axis मत कहिए।

और वो unifying line chapter से बाहर ले जाइए, क्योंकि यहाँ के लगभग हर लंबे जवाब के लिए यह पूरे मार्क वाला closing वाक्य है. हर command hormone के सामने एक feedback या antagonist signal होता है, जो internal environment को stable रखता है।

sections.title: Chapter cheat sheet: everything in one place

board_events.text: Chemical Coordination and Integration: the whole chapter on one board

COORDINATION: neural is fast, brief, local. Chemical is slow, lasting, widespread. The hypothalamus links the two. HORMONE: non-nutrient intercellular messenger, trace amounts, blood-borne, receptor-specific.

ANTERIOR PITUITARY (FLAT PiG): FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH, PRL, GH, plus MSH from the pars intermedia. POSTERIOR: stores oxytocin and ADH. GH: gigantism, acromegaly, dwarfism. ADH deficiency: diabetes insipidus.
PINEAL: melatonin, the body clock, the diurnal rhythm. THYMUS: thymosin, T-cell differentiation, atrophies with age.
THYROID: T3 and T4 (BMR; iodine + tyrosine), plus calcitonin (lowers Ca). PARATHYROID: PTH (raises Ca). PTH against calcitonin. Goitre, cretinism, myxoedema, Grave's, tetany.
ADRENAL CORTEX: aldosterone (Na and K), cortisol (glucose, anti-inflammatory), androgens. MEDULLA: adrenaline and noradrenaline, fight-or-flight. Cushing's, Conn's, virilism, Addison's.

PANCREAS: insulin (lowers glucose, beta), glucagon (raises glucose, alpha), somatostatin (delta). Insulin against glucagon. Deficiency: diabetes mellitus. GONADS: testis gives testosterone (Leydig) and inhibin (Sertoli); ovary gives estrogen (follicle) and progesterone (corpus luteum).
HEART: ANF lowers BP. KIDNEY: erythropoietin raises RBCs; renin runs the RAAS. GI: gastrin, secretin, CCK, GIP.
MECHANISM: water-soluble (peptide/amine), surface receptor, second messenger (cAMP), fast and short. Fat-soluble (steroid/thyroid), intracellular receptor, gene expression, slow and long.
ANTAGONIST TRIO TO NEVER FORGET: insulin against glucagon; PTH against calcitonin; oxytocin (ejection) against ADH (retention). Every command hormone is matched by a feedback or an antagonist signal.

segments.text: This is the whole chapter on one board. Not to learn it here for the first time, but to see, all at once, that it holds together.

Coordination: neural is fast, brief and local. Chemical is slow, lasting and widespread. The hypothalamus links the two. And a hormone is a non-nutrient intercellular messenger, in trace amounts, blood-borne, and receptor-specific.

The pituitary. Anterior, FLAT PiG: F S H, L H, A C T H, T S H, prolactin, growth hormone, plus M S H from the pars intermedia. Posterior stores oxytocin and A D H. Growth hormone gives gigantism, acromegaly and dwarfism. A D H deficiency gives diabetes insipidus.
Two quick glands. Pineal: melatonin, the body clock, the diurnal rhythm. Thymus: thymosin, T-cell differentiation, and it atrophies with age.

Thyroid: T three and T four for basal metabolic rate, built from iodine and tyrosine, plus calcitonin which lowers calcium. Parathyroid: P T H, which raises calcium. P T H against calcitonin. And the disorders: goitre, cretinism, myxoedema, Grave's, and tetany.

Adrenal cortex: aldosterone for sodium and potassium, cortisol for glucose and anti-inflammatory action, and androgens. Medulla: adrenaline and noradrenaline, fight-or-flight. Disorders: Cushing's, Conn's, virilism, and Addison's.

Pancreas: insulin lowers glucose from the beta cells, glucagon raises it from the alpha cells, somatostatin from the delta cells. Insulin against glucagon, and deficiency gives diabetes mellitus. Gonads: the testis gives testosterone from Leydig and inhibin from Sertoli; the ovary gives estrogen from the follicle and progesterone from the corpus luteum.
The organs that are not classical glands. Heart: A N F lowers blood pressure. Kidney: erythropoietin raises red cells, renin runs the R A A S. G I tract: gastrin, secretin, C C K, and G I P.

Mechanism, in one line each. Water-soluble, meaning peptide or amine: surface receptor, second messenger such as cyclic A M P, fast and short. Fat-soluble, meaning steroid or thyroid: intracellular receptor, gene expression, slow and long.

<excited>And the trio to never forget: insulin against glucagon, P T H against calcitonin, oxytocin ejecting against A D H retaining. Look back at that board one more time. Every command hormone on it is matched by a feedback or an antagonist signal. That is the chapter, and that is the body keeping itself steady.
यह पूरा chapter एक board पर है. इसे यहाँ पहली बार सीखने के लिए नहीं, बल्कि एक साथ यह देखने के लिए कि यह सब आपस में जुड़ा हुआ है।

Coordination: neural fast, brief और local. Chemical slow, lasting और widespread. Hypothalamus दोनों को जोड़ता है. और hormone एक non-nutrient intercellular messenger है, trace amounts में, blood-borne, और receptor-specific।

दो छोटी glands. Pineal: melatonin, body clock, diurnal rhythm. Thymus: thymosin, T-cell differentiation, और यह उम्र के साथ atrophy करती है।

Thyroid: basal metabolic rate के लिए T three और T four, जो iodine और tyrosine से बनते हैं, और calcitonin जो calcium घटाता है. Parathyroid: P T H, जो calcium बढ़ाता है. P T H बनाम calcitonin. और disorders: goitre, cretinism, myxoedema, Grave's, और tetany।
